summary.en: Haitian security forces have retaken the national stadium after two years of gang control and police killed a gang leader while intensifying operations against other sites, with kidnappings rising in Port-au-Prince. Salvadoran troops and missiles struck a gang hideout, destroying the Mawozo headquarters and killing about 20 gang members. Martine Moise, widow of the assassinated former leader, has registered to contest the presidential election. The United Nations warned that anti-gang operations must prioritise civilian protection. 193 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Haitiske sikkerhetsstyrker har gjenerobret nasjonalstadion etter to år med gjengkontroll, og politiet drepte en gjengleder mens de intensiverte operasjoner mot andre steder, med kidnappinger som øker i Port-au-Prince. Salviske tropper og missiler traff et gjengskjul, ødela Mawozo-hovedkvarteret og drepte omtrent 20 gjengmedlemmer. Martine Moise, enke etter den myrdede tidligere lederen, har registrert seg for å stille til presidentvalget. FN advarte om at anti-gjeng-operasjoner må prioritere sivile. 193 dødsfall knyttet til kamper ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Haitian conflict
background.extract: Since 2020, Haiti's capital Port-au-Prince has been the site of an ongoing armed conflict between rival gangs and the state. The government of Haiti and national security forces have struggled to maintain their control of Port-au-Prince amid this conflict, with gangs speculated to control up to 90% of the city by 2023. In response to the escalating fighting, an armed vigilante movement, known as bwa kale, also emerged, with the purpose of fighting the gangs. On 2 October 2023, United Nations Security Council Resolution 2699 was approved, authorizing a Kenya-led "multinational security support mission" to Haiti. Until 2024, the war was between two major groups and their allies: the Revolutionary Forces of the G9 Family and Allies and the G-Pèp. However, in February 2024 the two rival groups united in a coalition known as Viv Ansanm, formed to oppose the government and the UN mission.
